meaning: The difference between what a simulator produces and what the real robot and its surroundings produce. It covers physics, appearance and timing.
Moving a policy that was trained in simulation onto the real robot.
Bringing something real into the simulator. Examples are measured servo parameters, a scanned scene, or a policy trained on real data that is then tested in simulation.

A training method that draws each uncertain simulator parameter from a range at the start of every episode. If the ranges are wide enough, the real world falls inside the values the policy trained on.
Fitting a simulator's parameters to recordings of the real robot until the simulated motion matches the measured motion.
The system-identification toolbox that ships with MuJoCo 4.0. The SO-101 script built on it fits 24 servo parameters from one episode.
The step that tells the software which angle each joint's encoder reading stands for. On the SO-101 it is done by hand, and it can leave the gripper 10 to 20 mm or more off.
The tool at the end of the arm. On the SO-101 it is the gripper.
A policy is deployed zero-shot when it runs on the real robot with no further training on real data.
A control rule that pushes in proportion to the position error and brakes in proportion to the speed.
How hard a servo pushes per unit of position error. The model file calls it stiffness.
How hard a servo or a joint brakes per unit of speed.
Extra inertia at a joint that comes from the spinning motor and its gears.
A constant resistance inside a joint that the motor must overcome before the joint moves.

A fitting method for sums of squared misses. At each step it works out how each miss changes with each parameter, and then moves all the parameters at once to where the squared misses would be smallest.
The time a command takes to travel over the serial link to the servos.
A method that represents a filmed place as a cloud of small, soft, coloured blobs. The blobs are adjusted until pictures drawn from the cloud match the video frames.
A simulated copy of a real place, built from a video. Splats give its appearance, and a mesh gives the surfaces that objects collide with.
GPU units that accelerate ray tracing, covered in section 13. Isaac Sim's RTX renderer needs them, and the A100 and H100 do not have them.
The physics engine of NVIDIA's Isaac Sim. On PhysX, physics parameters are changed through the CPU.
One teleoperated recording made so that every fitted constant acts in the data. On every joint it includes small corrections, fast motion, starts and stops, and moves from rest.
Google DeepMind's suite of robot tasks built on MuJoCo. It ships the SO-101 pick-cube task and the system-identification script.
The Playground task that trains an SO-101 vision policy in simulation to pick a cube up. The policy is then deployed zero-shot.
The largest torque the simulated servo may apply, 2.94 N m. It is set from the 12 V servo's stall torque, and the fit does not change it.
The torque a motor produces when it is held still at full power. The servo datasheet gives this figure as the servo's strength.
An offset that the task adds to the simulated joint readings in each episode, to stand in for calibration error.
A 2024 suite for scoring real-robot policies in simulation.
NVIDIA's robot-learning framework, built on top of Isaac Sim.
NVIDIA's robot simulator. It renders through Omniverse RTX.
A 2024 method in which a language model writes the reward and proposes the domain-randomisation ranges.
An actuator model that is a neural network trained on hardware data. Isaac Lab uses it in place of an ideal PD loop.
A research pipeline that builds scanned scenes from a short video and tests policies in them.
In PolaRiS, a short fine-tuning of a policy on simulated demonstrations from other scanned scenes. It gets the policy used to how the simulator renders images.
A measure from -1 to 1 of how closely two sets of scores rise and fall together.
The GPU version of MuJoCo. Its batch renderer can ray trace splat files without RTX hardware.
The geometry type that Isaac Sim's scene files use to store Gaussian splats.
NVIDIA's code for reconstructing splats. It has a ray-traced method (3DGRT) and a rasterised method (3DGUT).
Another robot project. The SO-101 maker's model file adapts its motor parameters from it.
